questions.question: What must be true before a matrix can be symmetric in the usual sense?
options: It must have exactly two rows
It must have only positive entries

questions.question: For any real matrix $A$, the product $A^{T}A$ is always:
Why is every diagonal matrix symmetric?
options: The only possibly nonzero entries are on the main diagonal
All diagonal matrices have determinant $0$, in all instances without exception.

questions.question: For any square matrix $A$, which combination is guaranteed to be symmetric?
If $A$ and $B$ are symmetric matrices of the same size, what can be said about $A+B$?
options: It is always the identity matrix

questions.question: Which matrix is symmetric?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}4&a\\7&1\end{pmatrix}$ to be symmetric, what must $a$ be?
Is $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$ symmetric?
options: Yes, because its diagonal entries are real
No, because the diagonal entries differ

questions.question: What is the transpose of $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&5\\5&2\end{pmatrix}$?
Which value of $b$ makes $\begin{pmatrix}1&-3\\b&2\end{pmatrix}$ symmetric?
Why does the product of two symmetric matrices need not be symmetric?
options: The sum of symmetric matrices is never symmetric
The transpose of a product does not exist
Matrix multiplication may fail to commute
